html:
Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory of Australia, a tropical port on the Timor Sea. It is the country's closest city to Southeast Asia. In the Larrakia language its name is Garramilla.

Its land and harbour belong to the Larrakia people, with neighbours such as the Kungarakany, Awarai and Djerimanga inland and along the coast. HMS Beagle surveyed the harbour in 1839, and its crew named it Port Darwin after their former shipmate Charles Darwin.

South Australia, which then ran the Northern Territory, founded a town here called Palmerston in 1869. In 1872 the Overland Telegraph Line linked it to Adelaide, and a submarine cable to Java joined Australia to the world's telegraph network. A gold rush to Pine Creek followed, and a railway south was begun. Many Chinese came as miners and workers. The town was renamed Darwin in 1911, when the Commonwealth took over the territory.

Japanese planes bombed Darwin on 19 February 1942, the first and deadliest attack on Australia in the Second World War. On Christmas Day 1974 Cyclone Tracy destroyed most of the city, and it was rebuilt. Today it is a centre for the Top End, for mining and gas, and for Aboriginal communities across the north, including those of Arnhem Land.
sum: Darwin is the capital of the Northern Territory of Australia, a tropical port on the Timor Sea. It is the country's closest city to Southeast Asia. In the Larrakia language its name is Garramilla.
